title: Trenching: Spoil Piles, Ladders, Water, and Air Testing
summary: Cave-ins are the biggest risk in a trench, but falling spoil, water, bad air, and no way out also kill. Keep spoil back, provide a way out, and check the trench every shift.
talking_points: One cubic yard of soil can weigh as much as a car. Enter a trench only after protection against cave-ins is in place: sloping or benching, support systems, or a shield.
Keep spoil piles, materials, and equipment at least 2 feet from the edge, or use a retaining device so they cannot fall or roll in. Keep heavy equipment away from the edge.
Trenches 4 feet deep or more need a ladder, steps, ramp, or other safe way out within 25 feet of lateral travel for workers.

Stay out of a trench where water is collecting unless protections are taken, such as special support or shield systems, water removal, or a harness and lifeline. A competent person must monitor water removal equipment.

Test the air before entering a trench deeper than 4 feet where low oxygen or a hazardous atmosphere could be present, such as near landfills or stored hazardous substances. Keep rescue equipment ready and attended if hazards are present or expected.

Never work under loads handled by lifting or digging equipment. Stand away from trucks being loaded or unloaded. Use a warning system, such as barricades or signals, when mobile equipment works near the edge and the operator cannot see it clearly.
Do not work on the face of a sloped or benched trench above other workers unless those below are protected from falling material.

A competent person inspects the trench, nearby areas, and protective systems daily before work starts and as needed during the shift, and after rainstorms or other events that change conditions. If a hazard is found, workers leave the area until it is fixed.
site_hazards_to_check: Spoil piles or equipment closer than 2 feet to the trench edge
No ladder or ramp within 25 feet of workers in a trench 4 feet or deeper
Standing water or water collecting in the trench
Possible low oxygen or toxic gases in a trench more than 4 feet deep
Loose rock or soil on the trench face
Mobile equipment working near the edge with no warning system
Workers under raised loads or working above others on a sloped face
discussion_questions: Where is our spoil pile, and is it at least 2 feet back?
How do we get out of this trench in an emergency, and is a ladder close to everyone?
Did anyone check the air and the water in the trench before we went in today?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA Publication 2226, Trenching and Excavation Safety (2015). Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.
